### Summary

- Skill feature release: `bioresearcher-deep-research` 1.9.0 — optional map-first empirical cartography mode for category-discovery questions, plus three new manual agent-test cases (q08 offer, q09 taxonomy gate, q10 no-interview degradation).
- No connector rewrites, harness changes, or dependency pin changes; the repo version bump delivers the updated skill to plugin marketplace and connector users.

### bioresearcher-deep-research 1.9.0

- NEW optional `map-first` mode: empirical field cartography before plan review for category-discovery questions (taxonomy/landscape deliverables) - field-, community-, and question-agnostic across the biomedical realm. Adds `references/cartography.md` (primary vs context scope with interview elicitation, two-tier axis dispatch - scoped synthesis-mining + boundary-vocabulary focus axes, anti-pinned context archetypes, conditional venue-sweep remediation, anti-pinning contract with category anchoring rule, taxonomy merge + coverage audit, interaction matrix), a conditional map-first offer inside the Step 1 interview (fires ONLY on category-discovery-shaped queries; primary-scope confirmation when accepted), a Step 1.5 cartography dispatch block, taxonomy-based plan review (the taxonomy walk-through IS the plan review, non-waivable except by `no-interview`, which converts autonomously with rationale recorded in `assumptions.md`), cartographer-worker support in `references/worker-protocol.md`, optional report sections (landscape of unselected categories + decision guide by question scenario, default-on) in `references/report-template.md`, and cartography discipline in `references/analysis-methods.md`. The `bioresearcher-dr-worker` plugin agent conditionally reads the cartography reference for `cartography_*` focuses; shell workers are now told to anchor commands to the workspace root.
- Backward compatibility: with map-first OFF (not offered, declined, or inapplicable) every step, file, gate, and report section is unchanged - the offer question is the only default-mode addition and it fires only when the category-discovery heuristic matches. The existing deep-research agent-test suite (q01-q07) is untouched and remains the regression guarantee. Three new manual agent-test cases (q08 offer, q09 taxonomy gate, q10 no-interview autonomous degradation) use non-pharma topics to enforce mode genericity.

### Summary

- Repo-wide pin sweep to `biomcp@1.6.0`: bundled server configs, connector server pins, docs, agent-test MCP cases, and the vendored tool registry (43 core + 15 optional).
- **BREAKING**: the OpenCode connector is rewritten for opencode v2 ONLY — framework-based (`@opencode/plugin`), requires opencode >= 2.0.29; users on opencode v1 stay on `opencode-bioresearcher@1.11.1`.
- Agent-test harness and suites ported to opencode v2.
- Skill bumps: `bioresearcher-deep-research` 1.8.0 and `bioresearcher-onboard` 1.2.0.
- Demos: the `mcp-tool-tour-en/zh` true-run pack is re-captured at biomcp 1.6.0.

### bioresearcher-deep-research 1.8.0

- Pin sweep: prerequisites, recommended client command, and doctor check bumped to `biomcp@1.6.0` (43 core tools — `journal_metrics` and `preprint_fulltext` new; optional set and env gating unchanged).
- Response-envelope guidance updated for 1.6.0: `gene_diseases` without `DISGENET_API_KEY` silently returns OpenTargets rows (`source: "opentargets"`) — an `_error` row appears only when BOTH DisGeNET and OpenTargets fail; `batch_get` per-item failures are rows with `success: false` + `error` (batch continues); `patent_search` success is an envelope `{patents, total_hits, total_hits_basis, seminal_prior_art, mined_count, errors?, warnings?}` with backend failures riding in `errors` (no in-band marker rows, fallback notes in `warnings`).
- `drug_get`: `eu_regulatory` removed from the sections enum (requesting it fails with MCP -32602; documented as a troubleshooting row); `who_regulatory` reworded as WHO Prequalification products `{prequalified, products, note}`.
- Fulltext/preprint support: `article_get` `sections:["fulltext"]` documented (opt-in, never triggered by `"all"`; file-first — reply carries `file_path` + outline — with `fulltext_output:"inline"` + `fulltext_max_chars` 1000-200000, default 40000); `oa` corrected to license/access metadata only (statuses `open_access | free_to_read | paywalled | not_in_pmc | unknown`); `article_search` sources `preprint_only` (rows carry `preprint_server`, `ppr_id`) and `arxiv` (`arxiv_id`); `article_get` accepts preprint DOIs (`10.1101/YYYY.MM.NN.NNNNNN` and new `10.64898/*`).
- Other 1.6.0 truth updates: field contract heading raised to biomcp >= 1.6.0 and gains `journal_issn`; `gene_enrich` success shape `{pathways, total_reported, truncated}` + new `limit` param (1-100, default 30) + runtime guidance (15-45 s typical, ~105 s worst; client timeouts >= 120 s); `genbank_get` sequences over 1,000 chars default to a server-side file handle (`sequence_output:"inline"` opt-out); timeout table gains the 1.6.0 per-tool server deadlines; `OPENALEX_API_KEY` optional-auth row (`journal_metrics`).

### bioresearcher-onboard 1.2.0

- Pin sweep: vendored biomcp install pin bumped from 1.4.0 to 1.6.0 (`scripts/onboard.mjs` packagesToInstall and SKILL.md install description).
- OpenCode writer upgraded to the canonical opencode v2 shape: writes `mcp.servers.biomcp` (`type: "local"`, command `npx -y -p biomcp@1.6.0 biomcp`, `timeout` triple `{startup: 120000, catalog: 120000, execution: 120000}`); migrates a legacy flat `mcp.biomcp` entry (environment preserved, flat timeout N mapped to triple N, flat key removed) and leaves an existing canonical entry untouched.
- Re-bundled into the OpenCode connector as the MCP bootstrap: the v2 plugin no longer auto-registers biomcp programmatically (upstream `mcp.transform` is broken), so onboard now delivers that step.

### WorkBuddy Connector
- Migrate connector root icon from `icon.jpg` to 512x512 RGBA `icon.png` with anti-aliased transparency, satisfying WorkBuddy Connector Marketplace audit rubric F4 ("连接器根目录缺少 icon.svg 或 icon.png").
- Harden `scripts/ci/build-connector-workbuddy.mjs`: strictly disallow `icon.jpg`, validate 8-byte PNG signature (`89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`) and IHDR chunk (asserting exact 512x512 dimensions and 1KB-500KB size bounds), expand staging junk filter (`.git`, `.env`, `node_modules`, `*.pyc`, `*.swp`), and enforce post-tar content assertions.
- Harden CI smoke gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) to explicitly assert `bioresearcher/icon.png` inside the connector tarball and forbid `bioresearcher/icon.jpg`.
- Update `skills/bioresearcher-deep-research/scripts/markdown-to-html.py` to resolve `icon.png` across development repository and packaged connector layouts, dynamically embedding `image/png` data URIs.
- Update `demos/website/build.mjs` showroom assets to read `icon.png`, export `favicon.png` and `assets/icon.png`, and maintain backwards-compatible JPEG aliases for cached viewers.
- Update `AGENTS.md` and `docs/connector-workbuddy.md` documentation with icon provenance, dimensions, and sha256 hash.

### bioresearcher-deep-research 1.7.0

Citation integrity revamp from retrospective report on multi-entity toxin verification:

- `vet-references.py` tail isolation and locator replacement: splits trailing identifier tokens (`DOI:`, `PMID:`) from the right end of the citation line before replacing publication locators; targets the locator strictly in the pre-tail segment (`(?<=\.\s)...`), eliminating the locator-into-DOI splicing corruption on DOIs ending in year-like digits (`10.1248/cpb.27.1942.`) and enabling locator updates on citations with DOIs. Added Level 1 per-citation invariant checks (PMID/DOI verbatim preservation, structural DOI syntax validation) and Level 2 whole-document post-apply structural audit before writing to disk. Added `--diff` option for zero-dependency unified diff generation via `difflib`.
- `evidence-ledger.py verify` metadata conflict detection & author backfill: `cmd_verify` backfills missing authors from NCBI esummary and detects title token overlap (< 0.30) and DOI conflicts; conflicting records remain unverified with loud warnings and are never stamped `verified: true`. `vancouver_author` made idempotent on pre-formatted initials and punctuation (`"Chapman PB"` no longer truncates to `'Chapman P'`). `_esummary_locator` captures electronic article numbers from `elocationid` when page numbers are empty.
- PDB Dual-Entity support: `evidence-ledger.py` supports `pdb:` namespace and `ids.pdb` under `type: "dataset"`, canonicalizing PDB accessions, deriving `pdb:<PDB_ID>` keys, and rendering PDB dataset citations (`PDB structure <ID>: <title>. [Method] Resolution: <res>. URL`) without requiring article journal/locator fields. `references/worker-protocol.md` Rule 8 documents the dual-entity rule: cite PDB structures as `dataset` with `summary.title`; cite primary papers as `article` via `article_get(pmid)` (never copying PDB structure title/authors into article records).
- `evidence-ledger.py add` multi-format payload parsing: `_parse_payload` accepts JSON arrays, single JSON objects, and newline-delimited JSON (`.jsonl`) across `--stdin`, `@file`, and CLI arguments with markdown code-fence stripping, eliminating worker input crashes when piping JSON lines.
- Punctuation & double-period normalization: `_close_segment` ensures single-period termination on sponsor, status, organization, and update segments, eliminating `Sponsor: Tesaro, Inc..` double periods; `_author_list` terminates the author segment with a period (`, et al.` or `.`), aligning with Vancouver / NLM citation format.
- Protocol & anti-reading guidance: `SKILL.md` documents subagent tool inheritance (forbidding exploratory probe tasks) and adds an execution rule in the prompt template directing workers not to inspect script internals; `worker-protocol.md` provides explicit batch heredoc examples and CT.gov underscore status enum guidance.
- Orchestrator completion gate & dispatch hierarchy: `SKILL.md` Step 4 makes parallel worker dispatch (Tier A/B) mandatory whenever subagent tools exist, adds explicit `evidence-ledger.py check` execution per aspect upon worker return, formalizes the Remediation Worker protocol and prompt template with serialized ownership, and enforces a deterministic 2-retry circuit breaker.
- Warning disposition: `SKILL.md` Step 5c mandates that all warnings emitted during `verify` or `vet-references` must be resolved or explicitly justified in the report's Limitations section before Step 6.
- Prompt budget revamp: streamlined redundant interview/autonomy prose in `SKILL.md`, reducing prompt size from 498 lines to 411 lines (comfortably below the 500-line CI limit).
- Harness grader fix (`agent-test/run.mjs`): checks with `scope: "all"` evaluate over the parent stream when runs execute without subagents rather than falsely failing on missing subagent captures.

### bioresearcher-deep-research 1.6.0

Worker-friction fixes from live-run transcript forensics (three glm-5.3-flash agent tests; every fix traces to an observed failure):

- `check --markers <md...>`: worker self-gate closing the unbacked-marker hole (a negative-example `[@pmid:...]` cited in an aspect file without a ledger record passed `check` and nearly reached `render`). Mirrors render's group semantics exactly (all-cite groups must resolve via direct key or sec_index twin; mixed cite+non-cite groups fail; shape-kind tokens warn only; prose brackets and fenced examples ignored); missing marker files exit 1 (never a vacuous pass through the fail-safe catch); without `--markers` behavior is byte-identical.
- `render` warns (non-fatal) on hand-typed numeric citation brackets in the DRAFT - the observed `trials [1] [1-5]` leak class; link/wikilink/reference-def-safe pattern; fenced code excluded; render owns numbering.
- `verify` banner appends `; N already verified (not rechecked)` so dry-runs after `--apply` no longer read as "nothing checked".
- SKILL_DIR papercut fixed (4/6 dispatched workers failed their FIRST ledger command on `$SKILL_DIR` resolving to nothing): worker-protocol examples use the `<SKILL_DIR>` placeholder with "literal path string, NOT an environment variable" wording, and Tier B orchestrators substitute the resolved absolute path into every inlined `<SKILL_DIR>` so workers never see a placeholder.
- Worker protocol: re-add-is-safe upsert note (upsert merges fill-only - workers no longer grep the script source to trust re-adds, and cross-aspect keys are remedied by re-adding to the own ledger); `retrieved_at` must be the real UTC call time (`date -u`), never rounded/placeholder; query-parameter-derived values (e.g. a phase filter) may enter `meta` only with the filter captured in `provenance.args` and disclosed; markers are only for resolvable cited sources (mention-by-id stays plain text); end-of-aspect gate is now `check <file> --markers <aspect>.md`.
- New "Restart / gap top-up" protocol (serialized ownership transfer): codifies the observed-safe pattern of a top-up worker adopting a terminated worker's aspect - same ledger via `add`, targeted report edits, `check --markers`, never other aspects or the draft.
- Orchestrator duty: numeric caps from the user/plan are relayed to worker prompts VERBATIM (a live run's "at most 10 calls" became "roughly 8-14" and the worker made 24, causing a timeout).
- clinical-trials.md: CT.gov v2 status-filter enum documented (single value, any case, commas AND spaces fail with HTTP 400 - hit in three live runs).

### bioresearcher-deep-research 1.5.0

Citation-pipeline revamp: citations are key-based end-to-end and numbered nowhere until rendered - the ledger is the single source of truth and hand-assembled citations/bibliographies are structurally impossible instead of merely discouraged.

- New `evidence-ledger.py render` (the single numbering authority): orchestrator drafts `final_report.draft.md` with semantic cite-key markers (`[@pmid:21639808]`, groups `[@a; @b]`); `render` numbers every marker by first appearance (range-compressing groups), rewrites them in place, and appends the References section generated from the merged ledger via the same rendering path as `bib`. Marker tokens must be namespace+shape-valid cite-keys (prose `[@home]`/pandoc `[@Chapman2011]` brackets pass through verbatim); `doi:`/`pmcid:` markers resolve through the secondary-id index when merge promoted the twin to a `pmid:` key. Hard-fail contract (exit 1, output file never written): unresolved key (with did-you-mean suggestions), any record that would render `[MISSING ...]`, or re-rendering an already-rendered document.
- New `evidence-ledger.py check` (worker validity gate): re-reads/re-normalizes the ledger, prints counts + derived keys; exit 1 iff quarantined lines exist (zero-record evidence-gap-only ledgers legitimately pass). `add` now echoes the derived canonical k
